# Customer Review Analysis

**Prepared:** 21 Nov 2026 · **Data:** collected 21 Nov 2026 · **Reproducible:** every number below is regenerated by the scripts in [`scripts/`](scripts/) from the datasets in [`data/`](data/).

## 1. What was collected (and what was not)

| Sample | Platform | Selection | Size | Date range | File |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Google Play (India, English) | **Newest** reviews, paginated | **1,200** | 9 Jul – 20 Nov 2026 | `data/play_newest_1200.json` |
| B | Google Play | "Most helpful" sort (low-star filter requested; Play returned mixed ratings) | 450 | 30 May – 20 Nov 2026 | `data/play_most_helpful_450.json` |
| C | Apple App Store (India) | Public RSS feed, most recent, 10 pages | **500** | 10 May – 19 Nov 2026 | `data/appstore_recent_500.json` |
| — | App metadata | Play listing | — | 21 Nov 2026 | `data/play_app_metadata.json` |

- **Sample A is the primary dataset** (unbiased by helpfulness sort, most recent, largest). Sample B was used only for reading; it is not used in any percentage.
- **Reddit could not be accessed** from this environment (HTTP 403). Web search found no substantive Reddit threads; public complaint sites (consumercomplaints.in, voxya.com) were reviewed qualitatively (R-30, R-31). No Reddit claim is made.
- Reviewer names and avatars were **not collected**. Review IDs, dates, ratings, text and CD's reply are retained for traceability.
- We have **read and hand-reviewed all 480 one- and two-star reviews in Sample A** (412 of them have ≥25 characters) and all 153 one- and two-star reviews in Sample C. We have **not** audited "hundreds of thousands" of ratings; the lifetime histogram is used only as context.

### Context: ratings vs written reviews

| | Play lifetime ratings (683,627) | Play Sample A (written, newest) | App Store Sample C |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5★ | 76.6% | 42.4% | 50.2% |
| 4★ | 12.1% | 13.7% | 17.2% |
| 3★ | 3.5% | 3.9% | 2.0% |
| 2★ | 1.4% | 4.2% | 2.4% |
| 1★ | 6.4% | 35.8% | 28.2% |

Written reviews are far more negative than overall ratings: complainants write; satisfied customers tap stars. **The themes below describe what dissatisfied customers talk about; they do not measure how common a problem is among all customers.** That requires Country Delight's own contact-reason data (EV-055).

Month-by-month share of 1–2★ in Sample A: Jul 32% · Aug 44% · Sep 43% · Oct 41% · Nov (to 20th) 39%.

Country Delight publicly replied to **70%** of Sample A reviews (EV-058): an existing strength worth preserving.

## 2. Method

1. **Reading pass.** All 1–2★ reviews in Samples A and C were read in full to build the theme taxonomy bottom-up (13 negative themes, 8 positive themes). The research categories in the brief were treated as prompts, not as answers.
2. **Coding rules.** Each theme was written as an English + Hinglish keyword rule (`scripts/code_negative_themes.py`, `scripts/code_positive_themes.py`). A review can carry several themes.
3. **Validation.** A random sample of 30 coded negative reviews (seed 2026) was judged by hand: **63 of 72 theme assignments were correct (≈88% precision)**. Observed misses were mostly *recall* failures in delivery reliability ("haven't received", "two days no milk"), so **delivery-reliability counts are likely understated**. Two rule defects found in an earlier pass ("late" matching "later", "advertising" counted as an app issue) were fixed before the final run.
4. **Data-quality flag (App Store).** 11 App Store reviews (all 5★) contain unfilled template placeholders such as "[product]", "[easy/difficult]" and "[describe what they did]"; 85 of 337 App Store positive reviews share an identical title with another review. Positive-theme shares from the App Store are therefore reported with caution, and **Play is the primary source for what customers value**. No such duplication was found in Sample A.

## 3. Headline findings

1. **Customers love the product and the morning ritual.** In substantive 4–5★ Play reviews, quality/taste (55%), product range (52%) and reliable early delivery (38%) dominate. Self-serve subscription and vacation control is a named positive (16%). **These must be preserved, not "fixed".**
2. **Product quality/freshness/damage is the single largest complaint theme**: 26% of Play and 33% of App Store negatives. This *contradicts* the executive pitch's statement that customers "rarely complain about milk quality or freshness" (EV-061). An AI agent cannot fix the product; it can make **resolution** of a bad item faster and fairer (UC2).
3. **Two-thirds of negatives are about post-order workflows an agent can address.** 66% of coded Play negatives and 78% of App Store negatives mention at least one of: wallet/deductions/refunds, recharge/payment, offers/cashback, delivery reliability, support access, subscription/vacation control (EV-062).
4. **Trust in money movements is fragile.** Wallet/deduction/refund themes appear in 17% (Play) and 28% (App Store) of negatives, often framed as "fraud" or "loot" even where the published rules (VIP benefit caps, split cashback, 25–26 h Autopay lag) explain the event. **Explanation is the missing product, not the money.** (UC1, HY-001)
5. **Support access, not just support quality.** Customers cite no visible help, numbers that do not connect, bots that "go round and round with scripts", tickets marked resolved without resolution, and no language match. Several reviewers are explicitly hostile to bots ("put all in AI chat bots"). **A Graine agent must be visibly *more* capable than a tree and must always offer a human path.**
6. **Control over subscriptions is both loved and a pain point.** Positive reviews praise pause/vacation; negative reviews cite lost calendar views, vacation length limits, skips that skip two days, and items added without consent. **Changes must be explicit, confirmed and reversible** (UC5, HY-003).
7. **Outbound contact is already a complaint.** Repeated promotional calls (including "10 calls a day" and weekly calls adding items to the cart) appear in 2–3% of negatives (EV-068). Automating outreach without consent and frequency caps would **amplify** an existing harm. UC4 must be consent-first.
8. **Doorstep timing matters.** 5 AM bells, early-morning calls from delivery partners and items left outside recur (6–9% of negatives). The app already has "Call before delivery / Ring the bell / Voice instructions" preferences (EV-030), but they are buried. **A 4:30 AM voice call (as in the executive pitch) would be rejected by exactly these customers** (EV-066).

Several of these complaints are **explained by published rules** the customer did not understand at the moment of the event: VIP benefit caps (EV-010), offer voiding on change (EV-011), split cashback (EV-031), the Autopay lag (EV-009). That gap between rule and understanding is the core opportunity for a grounded conversational layer.

## 5. What customers value (preserve)

Substantive 4–5★ reviews (≥20 characters). Play n=298; App Store n=330 (see the caveat in §2.4).

| ID | Theme | Play | App Store | Design implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | Milk & product quality, freshness, taste | 55.4% | 39.1% | Keep the product at the centre of every screen and agent answer; surface Test Reports (EV-032). |
| P08 | Product range & groceries | 52.0% | 48.8% | Discovery help (UC3/UC6) should widen baskets without hiding the catalogue. |
| P02 | Reliable early-morning delivery | 38.3% | 55.2% | Do not disturb the morning ritual; no pre-dawn voice. |
| P07 | Value, VIP & offers | 36.2% | 18.2% | VIP is valued by many; explain it, don't push it. |
| P05 | Subscription & vacation flexibility | 16.1% | 19.7% | The existing self-serve UI works for many. **The agent is an option, not a replacement.** |
| P06 | Customer support helpful | 15.1% | 16.1% | Human support is praised by name; agents must hand off warmly. |
| P03 | Convenience & doorstep service | 12.8% | 31.5% | — |
| P04 | App ease of use | 7.0% | 4.5% | — |

Representative positives: "one of the best apps I have been using on time delivery and good packing and quality products" (Play · 2026-10-29 · 5★); "Their customer support is excellent… Milk and Paneer quality is top notch" (Play · 2026-08-11 · 5★); "I like how i can pause to modify milk quantity up until midnight for the next morning's delivery" (App Store · 2026-08-10 · 5★).

## 6. Testing the existing executive pitch (S5b) against this data

| Pitch statement | Our finding | Verdict | Register |
|---|---|---|---|
| "An audit of over 500 recent 1★ and 2★… reviews" | Dataset not supplied; our 633 negatives replace it | Replace with this analysis | EV-060 |
| "Customers rarely complain about milk quality or freshness" | Largest single negative theme (26% / 33%) | **Contradicted: withdraw** | EV-061 |
| ">80% of negative ratings stem from post-order workflow bottlenecks" | 66% Play / 78% App Store mention ≥1 workflow theme | Directionally supported; use measured figures | EV-062 |
| Support dead-ends ~30%, wallet/VIP ~25%, cutoff/doorstep ~35% | Support 18–33%; wallet+VIP 28–45% (overlapping); schedule+doorstep 20–24% | Category shares not reproduced | EV-062 |
| 4:30 AM stockout swap calls | Doorstep/early-call complaints recur; calls before 9 am carry regulatory risk | **Revise to WhatsApp/push, opt-in** | EV-066 |

## 7. Implications for the use cases

| Use case | Supported by | Strength of customer evidence |
|---|---|---|
| UC1 Wallet & Smart Recharge | N03, N04, N02, N05 | **Strong** |
| UC2 Delivery issue resolution | N06, N08, N09, N07 | **Strong** |
| UC3 In-app conversational agent | N09, N10, N11 | Strong for help/navigation; moderate for shopping |
| UC4 Offers & promotions outreach | N05 (offer clarity); **N13 is a risk** | Weak demand signal, **high governance need** |
| UC5 Conversational subscription management | N10, P05 | **Strong**, with the caveat that many customers already like the UI |
| UC6 Wellness & discovery | Existing health-goal merchandising (EV-036); no review demand signal | **Hypothesis**: validate with an experiment |

## 8. Limits

Keyword coding is approximate (≈88% precision; recall gaps in delivery reliability). English-language Play results only (Hindi in Latin script is captured; Devanagari and other scripts partially). Six-month window. Self-selected reviewers. No access to Country Delight's internal ticket data, which is the necessary next step to size each problem.
